verdict.rationale: Bitwarden documents its own programmatic vault surfaces. The official CLI is described as a fully-featured tool for "accessing and managing your vault", personal API keys are positioned for automated workflows, `bw serve` exposes the vault as a local Vault Management REST API with an OpenAPI document, and an official MCP server completed a live handshake. However, the evidence only shows querying of items and TOTP codes; creating or editing entries and seeding TOTP secrets programmatically are never explicitly documented. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of item create/edit commands or endpoints, programmatic TOTP-secret seeding, documented MCP-server write tools, and hands-on corroboration of agent-driven writes.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an agent can create and update vault entries — seeding new TOTP secrets, storing credentials — through documented programmatic surfaces

citations.quote: The Bitwarden command-line interface (CLI) is a powerful, fully-featured tool for accessing and managing your vault.
Using the personal API key for CLI authentication is suitable for automated workflows
documented `bw serve` mode exposes the whole vault as a local RESTful API (Vault Management API) an agent can query for TOTP codes and items
The Vault Management API page embeds its own OpenAPI document for the CLI's `bw serve` local server.
